The SR-556 is a semi-automatic AR-15 style rifle manufactured by Sturm, Ruger & Co. The rifle was introduced in 2009 in .223 Remington/5.56?45mm NATO and as a .308 Winchester AR-10 variant in 2013, the SR-762. It is one of several AR-15 rifles to use a gas piston operation. Ruger announced on May 15, 2009 on the SR-556 being produced, and in January 2016, Ruger discontinued all existing SR-556 rifles in preparation for a new takedown variant.
 Several of these rifles came to the Zone through the scientists. According to rumors, six small containers with these guns were sent from foreign sponsors to Professor Sakharov, but 5 of them were lost before arrival.

Shortened version of KS-23 with removable metal stock. 23mm Soviet multifunctional police pump-action shotgun, designed to suppress riots, selective force, mental and chemical effects on offenders. Interestingly, having a caliber of more than 20 mm and a rifled barrel, the KS-23 should not be classified as small arms, but as small-caliber artillery.\n %c[ui_gray_2]ATTACHMENTS: Boar Tactical Kit for KS-23M Drozd.

A 5.45mm Frankenstein's monster of a rifle designed by gunsmiths in the zone. It differs from the standard version by the installed parts kit, which includes a tactical pistol grip, a forend with Picatinny rails, and a folding telescopic buttstock, which significantly improves ergonomics of the gun. The kit also includes a laser targeting device, a tactical flashlight and an adapter mount for sighting devices. In the Zone, similar models are usually used by mercenaries and Ukrainian Spetsnaz for conducting special operations.

The AKS-74U was intended for use mainly by Spetsnaz units, airborne infantry, rear-echelon support units and armoured vehicle crews, who require a compact but relatively powerful individual automatic weapon. The AKS-74U is significantly more manoeuvrable in tight quarters than the AKS-74, but a significant decline in muzzle velocity resulted in a decrease in effective range. This special modified variant comes with a 45 round RPK magazine.

SA58 OSW (Operations Specialist Weapon) manufactured by American company DSA (David Selvaggio Arms) is a legal copy of the FAL, its made with the same Steyr-Daimler-Puch production line equipment as the StG-58. It may come with a different barrel length, an aluminum-alloy lower receiver, and improved Glass-filled Nylon furniture. Civilian models are semi-automatic, but military and Law Enforcement clients can procure select-fire models that have a fully automatic cyclic rate of 750 rounds/minute. The DSA-58 can use any metric-measurement FAL magazines.

Customized version of Makarov PM with longer threaded barrel for use with PMM silencer. This Soviet legacy is the most common pistol in the Zone and is one of the best compact self-defence handguns available. It is small, highly reliable, easy to use and maintain in working order. It also suffers from several drawbacks, including short range, low firing accuracy and poor stopping power, while also losing out to modern pistols in its class in terms of weight and magazine size. In 1951, the Pistolet Makarova was selected because of its simplicity, easy manufacturing, accuracy, and reasonable stopping power.\n %c[ui_gray_2]ATTACHMENTS: \n %c[d_purple] • %c[ui_gray_2] Silencer: Silencer PMM

This Soviet legacy is the most common pistol in the Zone and is one of the best compact self-defence handguns available. It is small, highly reliable, easy to use and maintain in working order. It also suffers from several drawbacks, including short range, low firing accuracy and poor stopping power, while also losing out to modern pistols in its class in terms of weight and magazine size. In 1951, the Pistolet Makarova was selected because of its simplicity, easy manufacturing, accuracy, and reasonable stopping power.

A relatively rare variant, the Makarov PMM was a redesign of the original PM. In 1990 a group of engineers reworked the original Makarov, primarily by increasing the load for the cartridge. The result is 25% more gas pressure, increasing muzzle velocity. The PMM's double-stacked magazine holds 12 rounds, compared to the PM's 8 rounds.\n %c[ui_gray_2]ATTACHMENTS:\n %c[d_purple] • %c[ui_gray_2] Silencer: Silencer PMM

The SIG-Sauer P220, manufactured in the late 1970s by J.P. Sauer & Son Company, is often considered the best out of the box .45 calibre double action pistol. An instant success, the P220 was adopted by the Swiss and Japanese SDF and by many European police organisations. This pistol also found its way into the US, first through the Browning Arms Company of Utah and since the 1980s, through the SIGARMS Company of New Hampshire.

 %c[d_purple] • %c[ui_gray_2] Silencer: BLACK BOX .45

Developed in Israel by Command Arms & Acessories (CAA), the AK-Alfa assault rifle was first presented to the public in 2016. This weapon is marketed under two brands - "Kalashnikov USA" and "Kalashnikov Israel". Apparently, this weapon got into the Zone with the the ISG fuction. The AK-Alpha assault rifle is an attempt to improve the ergonomics of the AK rifle while maintaining its main advantages - high reliability and ease of maintenance.
 The base for the AK-Alpha is the receiver, the barrel with the gas tube, the bolt group and the main components of the trigger of the Russian-made Saiga carbine.

 %c[d_purple] • %c[ui_gray_2] Silencer: 5.45/7.62x39 Hexagon Sound Suppressor

Korth is a high-end firearms manufacturer based in Lollar, Hesse, Germany. Builders in the tradition of ultimate European luxury brands, Korth are perhaps best known for revolvers with price tags that might as well be written in diamongs, though the entry point is far more accessible. The starting point for a Korth is around that of a Rolex: five thousand dollars. While a Korth PRS is basically a Colt 1911 remade with German engineering, making it compatible with the same parts, a particular oddity is its roller locking system with bolt head, reminiscent of HK handguns. With a single action trigger and a precision barrel, it is a very accurate and easy to shoot cousin of the 1911.
 This model has a four inches barrel and little more, just enough to get you started.
 %c[ui_gray_2]ATTACHMENTS:
 %c[d_purple] • %c[ui_gray_2] Silencer: none

The Howa Type 20 Assault Rifle, referred to as the Type 20 5.56mm Rifle, is an ambidextrous assault rifle resistant to corrosion for exposure to seawater, developed for the Japan Ground Self-Defense Force by Howa. A small arms test was made by the JGSDF in 2018 to compare the HK416, SCAR-L, and Type 20. All three rifles satisfied the JGSDF's requirements of better environment durability, fire power and extensibility over the then-in-service Type 89, but the Type 20 received the highest score. It is speculated that the design was influenced by Japan's experience of procuring and utilizing a number of foreign rifles, and has been compared to the HK433 and the SCAR.
 The J-3 high-power cartridge, a 5.56 mm round made to be powerful enough to penetrate modern body armor despite the rifle's relatively short barrel length, was developed specifically for the Type 20.
 It remains a mystery why, how, and in what quantity this rifle came to the participants of a scientific expedition to the Zone.
